title: European audiences stay loyal: Josephine Baker in Copenhagen
summary: He observes that Europeans still acclaim artists who were once great, as with an elderly Josephine Baker at the Tivoli.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I think -- I've always had the

opinion, and I think it's true, if you ever were something, particularly in Europe and overseas, you still are with those people. They're not fickle in their -- even though you haven't done anything for a long time, if you have done something that they acclaimed you for, they still do. I witnessed a performance of Josephine Baker, when I was over in Denmark. She was playing at the Tivoli in Copenhagen. And of course she was up there in years, and yet she -- while the performance was all right, I mean I can't see her getting the kind of acclaim for this performance if she had done it in the United States.

Because here was a very elderly lady up there doing her thing, which -- and the people just tore up the place. And I thought that was a good lesson about -- I've seen this happen with -- I don't even want to mention any names with this, because I've got some records of it, some of our older musicians have gone over there and they've played concerts and they've got records, and to hear the audience you'd think that this was the greatest thing that ever happened. And it was pretty pitiful. But because they had been great they were still accepted as being great, and I think that's a very nice thing about Europe, and I assume this is probably true elsewhere around the world, but particularly in Europe.
